139 /**
140 * @brief Check that that two generic objects are close, i.e. that their absolute difference is less than 1e-12.
141 *
142 * @tparam X Type of the first object.
143 * @tparam Y Type of the second object.
144 * @param x First object.
145 * @param y Second object.
146 * @return `::testing::AssertionSuccess()` if the absolute value of their difference is less than 1e-12.
147 * `::testing::AssertionFailure()` otherwise.
148 */
149 template <typename X, typename Y>
150 ::testing::AssertionResult generic_are_near(X const &x, Y const &y) {
151 double precision = 1.e-12;
152 using std::abs;
153 if (abs(x - y) > precision)
154 return ::testing::AssertionFailure() << "X = " << x << " and Y = " << y << " are different. \n Difference is: " << abs(x - y);
155 return ::testing::AssertionSuccess();
156 }
157
158 /// Macro that expects ::generic_are_near to return true.
159 #define EXPECT_CLOSE(X, Y) EXPECT_TRUE(generic_are_near(X, Y));
